title: Prime Predecessors with an Even Number of Prime Factors
main_claim: There are infinitely many primes p with p-1 squarefree and Omega(p-1) even, i.e. mu(p-1)=1.

issues.location: Sections 3, 5, 7 (Prop. sh:transference, sh:ideal; Lemmas ex:block-sieve, ex:proxies)
issues.description: The key graph-transference, ideal-operator, comparison-kernel, integer bilinear, block-sieve and proxy-discrepancy/density inputs are imported from the companion paper S and not reproved here. Their stated hypotheses match how they are used in this paper. Their correctness was not re-derived in this audit, which relies on the sibling audit of S (rank 73, no_gap_found).
issues.evidence: Section 3 states 'The graph transference and residual ideal operator are imported from [SmoothShifted]'. Section 7 imports S Lemmas 2.9, 7.3 and 7.4.

coverage:
Read the full LaTeX source (sections 01-07) and checked the following.

Weights (Sec 4): parity bookkeeping (r0 even, odd sign on the group part, so Omega(u) is odd and Omega(2u) is even); disjointness of the bands and groups; the midpoint-sum identity r0·sum m_j = L; the Delta/6 deviation budget in the mass lower bound; the tail lemma; the squarefree-loss ratio O(T L^-18).

Congruence theorem (Sec 6): the principal correction and the large-sieve algebra.

Long prime polynomial (Sec 2): the Linnik p-adic Vinogradov mean-value iteration (exponent recursion, Hensel count r^{K-k}, the r^{2s+K-k} factor); the log-phase estimate (Taylor remainder H^{-9/4}, box-occupancy exponent y - j/4 >= 5/16, Hölder giving the H^{-77/400} saving); the upper bound for D(s,chi); the Jensen/Blaschke local log-derivative; the de la Vallée Poussin contradiction 3/20 - 4/21 = -17/420; the contour shift with exp(-c·tau·T^2/2) beating every power of L.

Twisted correlation (Sec 3): shared-sign cancellation; small-mark extraction identity including damping; coprimality of r'/d' and r/d' for removing the rational centre; exceptional-interval count exp(O(L^b + L^{1-a} log L)); Gram-matrix sparse supremum; the three t-ranges.

Type II (Sec 5): allocation invariant and C_s > 88; Cauchy–Schwarz diagonal; the determinant identity mh' - m'h = k and its reverse bijection; matching the endpoint cores to the core form of the correlation theorem.

Extraction (Sec 7): presieve level; Buchstab identity and mesh; injectivity of (n,d) -> nd; box upper-sieve product V(W)^2 V(x^theta) with the mask expectation <= H_P; error exponents 0.64 and 0.20; balanced semiprime constant and the final kappa choice.

Not re-derived: the internals of the imported S results.
sibling_notes: Family 011 board had S (Weighted Dilation Graphs, rank 73) and the Poisson–Dirichlet paper (rank 62), both no_gap_found. This paper imports S Thm 3.5, Cor 3.11, Lem 3.4, Thm 4.1, Lem 4.2/4.3, Lem 2.9 and Lem 7.3/7.4 with matching hypotheses. The novel parts are: the prime long slot, which uses a self-contained weak zero-free strip; and the common parity twist, where eps(D_R)^2 = 1 at both ends. Both checked out.
